rationale: The book's core identification of righteousness as right-living (God as its measure; for creatures under authority, doing His commandments) best unifies the printed references, the garment of righteous acts, and the reckoning texts without collapsing the term into a pure forensic status that can exist independently of practice. Common interpretations rightly note gift/status language, yet the decisive texts (Deut 6:25; Ps 119:172; 1 John 3:7; Rev 19:8) define and identify the term with observed/done commandments and acts; Romans 4 and Phil 3:9 exclude works-as-debt and self-sourced claims while still counting faith that is inseparable from obedience (consistent with prior findings on belief and faith). Secondary elaborations on garments, washing, and armor are coherent extensions but not required for the core.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is right-living: God is Right-Living by definition (His ways/works the measure); for those under His authority it is the doing of His commandments (the law kept).
book_secondary_elaborations: Righteousness is given/reckoned by grace, not earned as a debt (Rom 4:4-8; Phil 3:9), yet the gift never renames wrong-living right.
The garment/fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints (Rev 19:8), granted then worn/kept/washed (Isa 61:10; Ezek 16; Zech 3; John 13; Rev 7:14; 3:4; 16:15).
Armor (breastplate of righteousness, helmet of salvation) is God's own war-dress (Isa 59) lent to the believer as conduct/Name covering.
Nakedness is exposure of covenant breach/sin; fig leaves are self-made coverings of human invention.
strongest_counter_interpretation: Righteousness primarily denotes a forensic/relational status of right standing before God (justification), in which God credits/imputes righteousness to the believer through faith in Christ (apart from works), with ethical conformity or righteous deeds as subsequent fruit rather than constitutive of the term itself.
counter_core_identification: Right standing before God received as a legal/relational gift by faith (imputed/declared righteousness), distinct from and prior to the believer's own right-living.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that the identity of righteousness (for those under authority) is the doing of the commandments/right-living; it treats practice as secondary fruit of a status that can be fully possessed without that doing.
counter_case: Romans 4:4-8 and Genesis 15:6 pattern: faith counted/imputed as righteousness to the ungodly apart from works, with forgiveness of sins as the content of the blessing.
Philippians 3:9: explicit contrast of 'mine own righteousness, which is of the law' vs. 'the righteousness which is of God by faith'.
2 Corinthians 5:21 and related Pauline texts commonly read as Christ becoming sin so believers become the righteousness of God (status exchange).
Isaiah 61:10 robe imagery often taken as covering that hides the wearer rather than acts the wearer performs; mainstream Protestant emphasis on imputation as the primary soteriological sense.
book_explanatory_advantages: Directly accounts for definitional texts that equate righteousness with observing/doing commandments (Deut 6:25; Ps 119:172) and with the one who does righteousness (1 John 3:7).
Preserves God's righteousness as His own right ways/works (Deut 32:4; Ps 145:17) without special pleading.
Explains Rev 19:8's plural dikaiōmata ('righteous acts') as the substance of the wedding garment without forcing a status-only reading onto an active plural.

Integrates reckoning language as grace that forgives and counts faith (never renaming wrong-living right) while remaining consistent with prior findings that saving belief/faith includes obedient submission.
Avoids inventing a righteousness that can be fully possessed by someone who does not do righteousness, which 1 John 3:7 explicitly rules out.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Foregrounds the strong Pauline 'apart from works' and 'counted/imputed' language that historically drove forensic readings of justification.
Offers a clean mechanism for how the ungodly can be justified without first achieving perfect obedience.
Matches the common Protestant symbolic reading of the robe as covering rather than performed acts.
decisive_sources: Romans 4:4-8 (works-as-debt excluded; faith counted; sins covered)
Philippians 3:9 (source contrast, not living vs. non-living)
unresolved_objections: Whether the 'righteousness of God' in Romans 1:17/3:21-26 is best glossed as God's own covenant faithfulness/saving justice (New Perspective) rather than either pure status or right-living.

Exact relation of imputed status language to the constitutive role of deeds: the book accepts gift/reckoning but insists the gift's substance remains right-living; some forensic systems treat deeds as non-constitutive fruit.
How far the garment/armor elaborations can be pressed without over-reading secondary symbols as definitional.
